newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges end week lower, cargoes steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges end week lower, cargoes steady.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel barges ended lower on Friday with some traders saying it was tracking lower swaps, but others saw it a temporary price cut to find buyers in a market idled by holiday.
High sulphur barges traded at $95 and $94.50 fob a tonne -- or $2/$2.50 a tonne lower than Thursday's highest trades -- after offers started higher at about $97/$97.50 early in the day.
Late talk was $94/$94.75 for material loading after August 21 and $95/$95.50 for prompter barrels, traders said.
Overall volume was very thin and some traders said that with many players absent from the market due to Assumption Day holiday sellers cut their price to find an outlet for some of their barrels.
"I think with return to normal business on Monday we will see a move to the upside," one trader said.
Others, however, saw the downside linked to lower swaps, with one trader saying: "Physical barges moved lower as swaps for September came down."
Many traders have said high sulphur barges have moved to levels unseen in months on the back of a shortage of prompt barrels but others said the oil was there but simply in storage.
